page: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the Dadsv7 family. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 32 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core, 256.0 GB of system memory providing 4.0 GB per core, and 3780 GB of local storage. The instance runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and supports Premium Storage. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong compute and memory capabilities. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng and the PassMark CPU score both rank in the top 10% tier. Multi-core CPU performance and PassMark extended instructions fall into the top 25% tier. Memory performance is also notable, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top 10% tier and memory bandwidth tests for both small cached and large uncached blocks scoring in the top 25% tier. For specialized tasks, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rank in the top 10% tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is in the top 25% tier.

The server demonstrates high efficiency for database operations, with PassMark database operations scoring in the top 10% tier and Redis SET operations reaching the top 25% tier. It is also capable of handling smaller artificial intelligence workloads, achieving top 10% tier speeds for prompt processing and text generation on small 135M LLM models. However, a key tradeoff is visible in larger workloads; prompt processing and text generation for large 70B LLM models drop to the middle 50% average tier due to the lack of dedicated GPU hardware. This makes the instance highly cost-efficient for high-density general-purpose workloads, database hosting, and web serving, rather than large-scale AI model training or heavy LLM inference.
description: Microsoft Azure D64ads_v7 is a general-purpose server instance from the Dadsv7 family, featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, the system includes 32 physical cores, 3780 GB of local storage, and supports Premium Storage under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It lacks dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmarks show top 10% tier performance in single-core CPU execution, PassMark database operations, and small LLM inference. Large block memory bandwidth and multi-core CPU performance rank in the top 25% tier. However, performance drops to the middle 50% average tier for large 70B LLM inference. This hardware profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense applications, making it highly suitable for database operations, web serving, and general-purpose enterprise workloads that require substantial local storage and balanced memory-to-CPU ratios without requiring GPU acceleration.
